title: Reading Transversal Angle Pairs
summary: Learn how to locate interior and exterior angles and recognize corresponding, alternate interior, and same-side interior pairs when a transversal crosses two lines.
statusText: These names describe where angles are located. Results connecting those positions to angle sizes come later.
statementLatex: \text{Two lines cut by a transversal form eight angles.}
learningObjectives: Identify a transversal and its two distinct intersection points with the crossed lines.
Separate the four interior angles from the four exterior angles.
Find the corresponding partner of any angle at either intersection.
Find the alternate interior and same-side interior partner of an interior angle.
Treat pair names as descriptions of position, not conclusions about angle sizes.
Preserve each classification when the diagram is tilted or reflected.

sections.title: Find the transversal
paragraphs: A transversal is a line that meets two or more other lines at distinct points. In the diagram, line t meets line ℓ at P and line m at Q, so t is the transversal.
The two crossed lines do not need to be parallel for these positional names to make sense. A later theorem may add parallel lines as a hypothesis.

sections.title: Locate interior and exterior angles
paragraphs: The four angles that face the segment from P to Q lie between lines ℓ and m. They are the interior angles.
The other four angles face away from that segment. They are the exterior angles for this transversal diagram.

sections.title: Match corresponding positions
paragraphs: Corresponding angles lie at different intersections and occupy matching corners. Imagine moving one intersection along the transversal to the other without turning the corner you selected.
Every one of the eight angles has exactly one corresponding partner at the other intersection.

sections.title: Cross for alternate interior angles
paragraphs: Alternate interior angles are both interior, lie at different intersections, and sit on opposite sides of the transversal.
Start by checking that both angles face the segment from P to Q. Then check that the transversal runs between them.

sections.title: Stay on one side for same-side interior angles
paragraphs: Same-side interior angles are both interior, lie at different intersections, and sit on the same side of the transversal. They are also called consecutive interior angles.
If the transversal runs between the two selected angles, the pair is not same-side interior.

sections.title: Keep names separate from results
paragraphs: These angle-pair names record position only. First ask whether the angles are interior or exterior, then compare their sides of the transversal and their corners.
The next lessons investigate what additional conclusions follow when the crossed lines satisfy further hypotheses.
